faq.question: Can I choose to do 1 or 2 actions on each of my turns during the Action phase?
faq.answer: Yes. On each individual turn, you can choose to take either 1 or 2 actions. You make this decision fresh each turn.
faq.source_quote: In the Action phase, players take turns doing 1 or 2 actions, going around the table until everyone has passed.

faq.question: When a global parameter reaches its goal, do I still get TR if I somehow raise it further?
faq.answer: No. Once a global parameter has reached its goal, you can't raise it any further, and raising that parameter no longer increases your TR.
faq.source_quote: When a global parameter has reached its goal, it can't be raised any further, and so does not increase your TR.

faq.question: Where does the generation marker track time—is it placed on the TR track?
faq.answer: The generation marker measures time (in rounds) and advances by 1 each round. It is not placed on the TR track.
faq.source_quote: The generation marker measures time (rounds) and starts at 1, moving up on the TR track.

faq.question: If I can't raise the oxygen level when placing a greenery tile, do I still place the tile and get its placement bonus?
faq.answer: Yes. You still place the tile and receive any placement bonus even if you can't raise the oxygen level; you just don't gain the TR increase.
faq.source_quote: If you can't raise the oxygen level you don't get the increase in TR either.

faq.question: Can Noctis city be placed next to other cities?
faq.answer: No. Noctis city must be placed on its reserved area and, like all cities, cannot be placed adjacent to another city.
faq.source_quote: May not be placed next to another city (exception: Noctis city must always be placed on its reserved area).

faq.question: How can I tell the difference between resource icons that mean cubes and resource icons that mean production?
faq.answer: Plain resource icons refer to resource cubes you have, while resource icons inside brown boxes refer to production of that resource.
faq.source_quote: In the game, resource icons refer to resource cubes, while resource icons inside brown boxes refer to production of that resource (see the project card below).

faq.question: When do I convert leftover energy into heat during the production phase?
faq.answer: At the beginning of the production phase, you convert leftover energy into heat; after that, you add resource cubes equal to your production.
faq.source_quote: During the production phase you add resource cubes equal to your production.

faq.question: What's the difference between a blue-ribbon effect and a blue-ribbon action?
faq.answer: Blue-ribbon boxes contain either an ongoing effect (always active) or an action (which you can use once per generation). The card will specify which.
faq.source_quote: Effect / action: Boxes marked by a blue ribbon show an ongoing effect or action that may be used during the game.

faq.question: When do I pay 3 M€ per card during setup—before or after I receive my starting resources?
faq.answer: You first reveal your corporation and receive your starting resources and production. After all players have done this, you then pay 3 M€ for each card you keep.
faq.source_quote: In player order, players then reveal their chosen corporation, get their starting resources and production (if any), and then pay 3 M€ for each project card they keep.

faq.question: How do I set up my production at the start of the game?
faq.answer: You start with 1 production of each resource, so place your player markers on '1' for each of the six production tracks (in the standard game only).
faq.source_quote: You start with 1 production of each resource on the player board, so place player markers on the tracks (only in standard game.)

faq.question: Can I take 0 actions on my turn, or do I have to take 1 or 2?
faq.answer: On your turn, you can take 1 or 2 actions, or you can pass (take no actions), which removes you from the round for the rest of the generation.
faq.source_quote: You can choose to take 1 or 2 actions on your turn.

faq.question: Does the action phase continue until everyone passes, or does something happen before the production phase?
faq.answer: The turns continue around the table until everyone has passed, and then the production phase begins.
faq.source_quote: And so the turn continues around until everyone is out by doing no actions.

faq.question: When a card triggers multiple effects, can I choose the order to perform them?
faq.answer: Yes. You may perform these effects in any order you choose, so long as all effects are completed before your action ends.
faq.source_quote: These effects (and other effects triggered by the card you just played) are performed in any order you choose.

faq.question: The rulebook mentions both 'red frame' and 'red border'—which term is correct?
faq.answer: The correct term is 'red border.' Resources or production with a red border means you can affect any player you choose, including yourself.
faq.source_quote: Resources or production with a red frame means that you can affect any player you choose (even yourself).

faq.question: What does it mean when the rulebook says 'Red-bordered resources are optional'?
faq.answer: You can choose whether or not to apply a red-bordered resource or production effect, including whether to target yourself or other players.
faq.source_quote: Red-bordered resources are optional, so card C does not remove your own plants, even if you are the only player that has any plant resources.

faq.question: What does it mean for an ongoing effect to 'trigger at any time'?
faq.answer: Ongoing effects on active cards activate at the specified times (not at the player's discretion). Actions, by contrast, can be used whenever you choose, like corporation actions.
faq.source_quote: Active cards (blue, D, E) have ongoing effects that may trigger at any time, or actions that you can use (just like the corporations).

faq.question: When I sell patents and discard cards, how much M€ do I get?
faq.answer: You gain M€ equal to the number of cards you discarded. For example, if you discard 3 cards, you gain 3 M€.
faq.source_quote: Sell patents: You may discard a number of cards from hand to gain the same number of M€.

faq.question: What's the exact sequence of events when all three global parameters reach their goals and the game ends?
faq.answer: The game ends after this sequence: the current production phase completes, players have one extra chance to convert plants into greenery tiles (in player order; this may trigger other effects such as placement bonuses), and then final scoring takes place.
faq.source_quote: When all three global parameters (ocean, temperature, and oxygen) have reached their goals, the game ends at the end of that generation.

faq.question: Where can I find the explanation of symbols in the rulebook?
faq.answer: If you don't understand the symbols on a card, read the explanation in parentheses on the card or see pages 14–15 in this rulebook.
faq.source_quote: If you don't understand the symbols - read the explanation in parenthesis on the card, or see page 14 & 15 in this rulebook.

faq.question: How do I determine where to place the 2 neutral city tiles at the start of the game?
faq.answer: Reveal and discard the 4 top cards of the deck, then use their cost numbers to determine where to place the 2 neutral city tiles on the map, each with an adjacent greenery tile.
faq.source_quote: Before you choose your cards, place 2 neutral city tiles on the map with an adjacent greenery tile each (these tiles are not yours, and do not increase the oxygen level): reveal and discard the 4 top cards of the deck and use their cost numbers to determine the positions of the tiles.

faq.question: Can I steal from the neutral opponent or reduce their resources?
faq.answer: You have a neutral opponent from whom you can steal resources or reduce any kind of resources and production.
faq.source_quote: You have a neutral opponent that you can steal from, or reduce any kind of resources and production from.

faq.question: Which direction do I pass cards during the card draft?
faq.answer: Each player passes their remaining cards to the next player (the direction alternates by generation according to the rules).
faq.source_quote: Each player first gets 4 cards and chooses one to draft, putting it aside and passing the rest to the next player.

faq.question: The rulebook says to pass 'to the left' but also says passing direction changes—which is right?
faq.answer: Pass to the next player, not always to the left. The direction alternates by generation (clockwise for even generations, counter-clockwise for odd).
faq.source_quote: Then you have 3 cards; set aside 1 of them and pass the rest to the left.

faq.question: Can I always convert 8 plants into a greenery tile, or only in certain situations?
faq.answer: As an action, you may convert 8 plant resources into a greenery tile and place it on the board, provided you have 8 plants and a valid placement location.
faq.source_quote: As an action, 8 plant resources can be converted into a greenery tile that you place on the board.

faq.question: What does it mean that a greenery tile 'must be placed next to another tile you own if possible'?
faq.answer: You must place the greenery tile adjacent to another tile that you own, but only if an empty area next to one of your tiles is available.
faq.source_quote: The tile must be placed next to another tile that you own if possible.

faq.question: When a card removes red-bordered resources, can I target myself?
faq.answer: Yes. A card that removes red-bordered resources may remove those resources from any player, including yourself (this effect may also be performed partly, or not at all).
faq.source_quote: A card that removes red-borded resources, may remove those resources from any one player (this effect may also be performed partly, or not at all).
